rule: Make money: grow the agent account with a positive expected return and controlled drawdowns. No target amount and no end date. SPY buy-and-hold is the yardstick results are reported against, not a target.
source: Owner 11/07: "Forget about the date target + target amount. Instead just focus on making money"

rule: At most the money in the MCP agent account (started with $2,000; now its balance). No transfers in or out.
source: Owner 11/07: "At most is the money on the mcp account and no transfers"; "2k budget"

rule: No margin borrowing; the agent account only (••••5318), never the owner's other accounts.
Kill switch: a KILL_SWITCH file (or the owner's word) stops all orders. Only the owner removes it.
Never deposits, withdrawals, account-setting changes, crypto or shorting. No banking or credit tools.
Pattern-day-trader guard: the account is limited-margin under $25k, so no more than 3 day trades in 5 business days. For now the code refuses all same-day round trips.
source: Account type checked 11/07; FINRA PDT rule

rule: Every real order goes through the order gate: confirmed by the pre-close run that day before 15:50 ET, a limit order at the broker's live quote, one ticket per order. No daily fill cap.
source: Owner 11/07 (fill cap removed); enforced by live.py

rule: At most 4 open positions; never average down.
Allowed by the account: stocks and ETFs (fractional), long calls and puts, and at Level 2 covered calls and cash-secured puts. Spreads need Level 3, which only the owner can request.
Current default until the strategy research adopts a change: buying options only (no selling to open, no multi-leg, no exercise; close before expiry); idle money stays in cash.
source: Owner 11/07: "you need to figure out the best option"; RULES.md

rule: Anthropic-linked ideas (ANT included once it lists) are allowed when the evidence supports them: public information only, the conflict disclosed, and the red-team checks for optimism bias.
source: Owner 11/07: "if the data recommends moving on these do it"; playbook.md

rule: Each order's thesis states its size and why. Sizing for a tested edge uses Kelly from its tested payoff distribution (sizing.py), planned at half-Kelly; one contract only when full Kelly covers it.
Theme caps at cost: AI/semis at most 40% of equity, energy at most 40%; leveraged ETFs at most 15% each.
No bet sized to chase a target: with no date target, variance bets without an edge are retired.

Options: open interest at least 1,000, spread at most 5% of the mid (10% for commodity or sector ETFs), delta 0.30-0.45 (never below 0.25), expiry 2-5 weeks, no entry within 3 days of expiry; sell at least one session before expiry.
Event premium only at the print day's 14:43 decision, when the implied move is at most 0.9x recent reactions; sell the next day.
An edge counts only if it comes from a committed script or a cited published study, tested before the decision; our own trades count only with their sample size.

Retired as tested and failed: the midterm rally, the Halloween effect, the turn of the month, RSI(2) dips, a follow-through day as an edge, "IV is low", the pre-earnings run-up through calls, FINRA short-volume spikes, Wikipedia attention, the put/call ratio, dip-buying calls after a -4% day.
Consensus check: if the idea is what any AI would suggest, it needs a measured edge.

Earnings-drop put (C1): a large company down 8% or more vs its pre-earnings close at the reaction day's 14:43 check; 1 put at delta 0.30-0.45, IV at most 1.3x the pre-print 20-day realized vol, spread at most 5%, OI at least 1,000, expiry at least 14 days, sized by Kelly.
The exit plan is written at entry. One contract sells all at +50%, two or more half at +50% and the rest at +100%, as a resting sell order at the broker; the stop moves to cost after a check at +40%.
Stops at the price where the thesis is wrong, with a -50% premium backstop, checked at the 14:43 check; a breached stop sells the same day.
Earnings-drop puts: hold 5 sessions with the -50% backstop; no take-profit.
Evening and Sunday runs propose; the 14:43 run decides on fresh prices before 15:50 ET; anything unconfirmed does not fill. The pre-open run never confirms or places.
Buys of 20% of equity or more (or a leveraged ETF) need a fresh risk red-team; every evening draft is red-teamed.
Prices come from verified feeds or the broker's live quote, never typed in; the ledger and journal are append-only, with a reason and a price source for every order and fill.

Any rule except the owner's limits can change: a proposal with evidence, a fresh red-team, adoption with a dated log entry (usually at the Sunday review), and this list updated the same day. A rule that keeps failing its own test is retired the same way.
source: Owner 11/07: "evolve the rules as we learn"; RULES.md

rule: Hold an S&P 500 ETF for the equity premium, possibly with a trend filter (above the 200-day average, else a T-bill ETF), instead of sitting in cash.
source: Strategy v2 claims S1, S2, S4

rule: Park idle cash in a T-bill ETF (SGOV or BIL) to earn the T-bill rate.
Sell cash-secured puts or covered calls where the account size allows, to earn the volatility premium instead of paying it.
source: Strategy v2 claims P1, P2 (P3: spreads, if the owner requests Level 3)

rule: Check stops during the day as well as at 14:43, and allow up to 3 same-day exits in 5 days for risk (the PDT limit).
Entry checklist: "Who loses from today's news, and how much of the underlying do they weigh?"
Anthropic-linked trades: the IPO timeline, base rates and any tested halo effect.
